terra.problem: Saying nobody is singing goes beyond the text. The verse does not mention singing.
Stumbling does not necessarily mean falling, and the verse distinguishes stumbling by day from the prophet stumbling by night. 'They all go down together' changes the picture.
The statement about what priests were supposed to do adds a Bible fact from outside this passage without a reference.
The drawer-for-a-quarter joke contradicts Papa Dorin's backstory. Mother Miller bought him for a quarter from a bin, not by trading a drawer.
The verse says both will be punished for their ways and repaid for their deeds. It does not say they receive the same treatment.
The verse says they will eat but not be satisfied. It does not specify a plate, physical fullness, or that this will never happen.
Comparing the stated suffering to wanting another cookie makes light of the consequence, even though the explanation then calls it serious.
The absolute claim that wood has never answered anybody goes beyond the passage, which says their divining rods inform them.
The statement that captivity comes up elsewhere in Scripture needs a reference.
Telling the baker to listen to the command not to go to these places applies the warning directly to the baker, although the passage does not identify the baker as its audience.
The claim that Joppa and Tarshish are places in Scripture is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The claim that Hebron and Bethlehem are towns is a Bible fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.

The statement about what sacrifices are supposed to do adds an unsupported generalization and can suggest that the sacrifices in this verse were intended to honor the LORD, which the passage does not say.
The verse says the sacrifices will bring shame; it does not say that peace will not follow.
